title: Closed points and Noetherian local models in a finite-residue tower
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $p:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $e:D\to C$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], both locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $y\in D$ and $x=e(y)$. Assume that the actual residue-field extensions $k\to\kappa(x)$ induced by $p$ and $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ induced by $e$ are finite-dimensional [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension]. Then $x$ is closed in $C$ and $y$ is closed in $D$ [def-weil-closed-points]. Moreover, $C$ and $D$ are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. There exist affine open neighbourhoods $U\subseteq C$ of $x$ and $V\subseteq D$ of $y$ such that $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_C)$ and $S=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_D)$ are Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Writing $\mathfrak p_x\subset R$ and $\mathfrak q_y\subset S$ for the primes corresponding to $x,y$, the germ maps induce isomorphisms $R_{\mathfrak p_x}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{C,x}$ and $S_{\mathfrak q_y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{D,y}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and both stalks are Noetherian local rings. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, algebraic closedness of $k$, or etaleness of $e$ is assumed.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre), closedness in the fibre and ascent over a closed base point; Morphisms Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), twice. For the affine-local presentations: Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), clause (6), and Algebra Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), localization clause. This isolates old Steps 4--6 of lem-trf-etale-completed-local-ring-iso.

proof.text: Every ideal $I$ of the field $k$ is either $(0)$ or $(1)$: if $0\ne a\in I$, then $a^{-1}a=1\in I$. Thus every ideal is finitely generated, so $k$ is Noetherian. The single affine open $\operatorname{Spec}k$ covers itself and has ring of sections $k$. By the definition of locally Noetherian this makes $\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01OV (definition-noetherian), affine neighbourhood definition; Algebra Tag 00FM (section-Noetherian), first paragraph

proof.text: Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to $p:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, using Step 1 and the assumed local finite type of $p$. It gives local Noetherianity of $C$. Apply the same lemma to $e:D\to C$, whose target is now locally Noetherian and which is locally of finite type by hypothesis. It gives local Noetherianity of $D$. Both applications use the local conclusion; no quasi-compactness is needed.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), locally Noetherian case, applied twice

proof.text: Let $s$ be the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [def-weil-residue-field], its residue field is canonically $k$ and the residue map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ of $p$ is the structural extension assumed finite in the statement. Apply [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre] to $p$ and $x$: the local finite type and finite residue extension hypotheses both hold, so the induced point of $C_s$ is closed. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $C_s\to C$ is a homeomorphism onto $p^{-1}(s)$. Since the base has just one point, $p^{-1}(s)=C$, and therefore $\{x\}$ is closed in $C$.

Apply [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre] to $e$ and $y$, using $x=e(y)$, the assumed local finite type of $e$, and the assumed finiteness of the actual residue map $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$. The point of $D_x$ induced by $y$ is closed. The homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies this with closedness of $\{y\}$ in the subspace $e^{-1}(x)$. Since $\{x\}$ is closed by Step 3 and $e$ is continuous, $e^{-1}(x)$ is closed in $D$. A subset closed in a closed subspace is closed in the ambient space: writing $\{y\}=F\cap e^{-1}(x)$ with $F$ closed in $D$ proves $\{y\}$ closed in $D$.

source.place: Tag 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre), closedness ascends over a closed base point by elementary topology; Schemes Tag 01K1

proof.text: By [pqf-def-locnoeth], each scheme in Step 2 has an affine open cover with Noetherian section rings. Choose a member $U$ of such a cover of $C$ containing $x$, and a member $V$ of such a cover of $D$ containing $y$. Then $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_C)$ and $S=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_D)$ are Noetherian by the choice of the covers. Only these two members are chosen; the covers need not be finite and no assertion about intersections of affine opens is used.

source.place: Tag 01OV (definition-noetherian), choosing the affine neighbourhoods in its definition

proof.text: Apply clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] first to $(C,U,x)$ and then to $(D,V,y)$. The opens are affine and contain the indicated points by Step 5. It gives exactly the germ-induced isomorphisms $R_{\mathfrak p_x}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{C,x}$, $r/s\mapsto r_xs_x^{-1}$, and $S_{\mathfrak q_y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{D,y}$ with the analogous formula. In particular these are presentations of the actual structure-sheaf stalks through the chosen section rings.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), clause (6), and the open-subspace stalk identification of Tag 01HF

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] for each germ localization in Step 6. Its source rings $R,S$ are Noetherian by Step 5 and the required localization conditions are precisely those supplied in Step 6, so the actual stalk rings $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ and $\mathcal O_{D,y}$ are Noetherian. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], localization at a prime is a local ring; the isomorphisms of Step 6 therefore also make these stalks local rings. This supplies both Noetherian local rings and the asserted germ-localization presentations.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), localization clause; Tag 07BH (section-local-rings), localizations at primes

The statement is true and unchanged. Stacks sources checked: 01TE (Morphisms, morphisms.tex:3565) for closedness in the fibre, with part (2) closing over a closed base point by elementary topology as Steps 3-4 write out; 01T6 (Morphisms, morphisms.tex:2765); 01OV (Properties, properties.tex:421). Step 1 (elementary): a field is Noetherian, and Spec k is a one-member Noetherian affine cover, so it is locally Noetherian. Step 2 applies pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft (Mathlib leaf) to p and then to e. Steps 3-4 use the same-unit lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre and the homeomorphism onto the preimage in def-pc-scheme-fibre: p^{-1}(s)=C makes x closed, then e^{-1}(x) is closed and y is closed in it. Step 5 (elementary) picks a cover member through each point from pqf-def-locnoeth. Step 6 is clause (c) of lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization (localization at the prime via the germs). Step 7 uses lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian with S = R minus p_x, and locality from def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime. proof_deps equal the union of the step uses. No SGA is cited, no off-unit statement needs a tool_use, and there is no cycle. Duplicate search (01TE/01TF/01T6 and stalk-Noetherian nodes) found none: lem-kun-closed-point-field needs finite type, and lem-sbc-composite-fibre-local-models is about fibre stalks. The sole citer, lem-trf-etale-completed-local-ring-iso at its Step 4, satisfies the hypotheses. Edge cases: identity of Spec k, purely inseparable k'/k, k[eps], infinite disjoint unions, the generic point of A^1 (excluded by the hypothesis), and empty schemes.
